passage:
The school made a new rule: students could not use phones during lunch. Many students were unhappy. They said lunch was their free time.
For the first few days, the cafeteria felt strange. Students looked around with nothing to do. Then conversations began. Some played word games. Others talked with classmates they had never spoken to.
Not everyone loved the rule, and some still wanted their phones back. But teachers noticed that students finished eating more slowly and left fewer lunch boxes unfinished.
After a month, the school changed the rule slightly. Phones were allowed on Fridays only.
The rule did not make everyone happy, but it helped students remember that free time can be shared, not only scrolled.
